entrypoints.summary: Kyber decapsulation invoked on attacker-forged ciphertexts when the attacker can observe its duration.

negative_controls: No crystals-go-specific timing trace or observed execution result is present in this bundle.
The public KyberSlash2 demo concerns end-of-November-2023 Kyber reference code on Arm Cortex-M4, not crystals-go.
observability.positive_marker: A timing difference that distinguishes the decryption outcome for malicious ciphertexts.

preconditions: The attacker can submit forged Kyber ciphertexts to decapsulation.
The attacker can observe decapsulation timing on a platform where the leakage is measurable.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Pairs of malicious Kyber ciphertexts derived from messages differing in one bit and attacker-selected parameters, as described for the shared KyberSlash2 attack.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit forged ciphertexts designed to induce distinguishable decapsulation timing outcomes and compare timings.

relation_candidates.rationale: The advisory conditions impact on an attacker being able to time Kyber decapsulation on forged ciphertexts.
The paper explains that differing decapsulation times distinguish decryption outcomes and can be iterated to learn secret coefficients.
The maintainer advisory describes possible learning of parts of the secret key under the timing precondition.
PR #21 states that it fixes KyberSlash2 by forcing certain divisions to be constant time.

impact.affected_asset: Kyber secret key held by the crystals-go decapsulation implementation
impact.attacker_capability: Possibly learn parts of the Kyber secret key by timing decapsulation of forged ciphertexts on affected platforms
impact.security_effect: Timing side-channel disclosure of secret-key material

causal_trace.summary: An attacker submits forged ciphertexts for Kyber decapsulation and can time the decapsulation operation on an affected platform.

The required constant-time property is broken when secret-derived values reach divisions whose execution time varies with their numerator; the patch record states that selected divisions had to be forced constant time.

The shared KyberSlash2 analysis identifies variable-time processor division in ciphertext compression (with public denominator 3329) as the timing-producing operation. The supplied artifacts do not include a crystals-go-specific pre-patch assembly trace tying its Go source to that instruction.
Timing distinctions during forged-ciphertext decapsulation can reveal plaintext-checking information; the crystals-go advisory bounds target impact to possible learning of parts of the secret key.

failure.operation: Variable-time division during ciphertext compression in the shared KyberSlash2 mechanism

primary_invariant.statement: Secret-derived values processed during attacker-timed Kyber decapsulation must not execute variable-time division operations.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The patch author reports that certain divisions required forcing to constant time, while the shared KyberSlash2 analysis attributes timing leakage to variable-time division on secret-dependent values.

quality.review_notes: Maintainer evidence establishes affected scope, attacker condition, and that PR #21 forces selected divisions constant time. The paper and demo establish the shared KyberSlash2 timing/key-recovery mechanism, but their demonstrated complete-key recovery is for reference-derived implementations on named Arm targets, not a crystals-go-specific run. The bundle lacks raw before/after poly.go lines and target-specific compiler/assembly or timing evidence; no executable target-specific harness is established.

remediation.invariant_restored: Selected divisions in the Kyber compression paths are forced to execute in constant time so secret-derived processing does not expose division-latency variation.
mitigation_classes: replacement or forcing of selected division operations

target.component: Kyber decapsulation and ciphertext-compression division handling (poly.go patch series)
